points.what: North America orders rose 33.2% to 261, contributing 65 of the 50-order weekly increase, or 130% of the total change.
points.so_what: North America alone more than accounts for the week's order growth, offsetting declines elsewhere.

points.what: Search orders grew 6.6% to 728, contributing 45 orders, or 90% of the weekly change, and holding a 70.7% share.
points.so_what: The week's growth rests on the largest source, so total orders track closely with Search.

points.what: APAC orders fell 2.0% to 446 and EMEA fell 4.2% to 184, contributing -9 and -8 orders respectively.
points.so_what: Both regions still grew 83.5% and 78.6% year on year, above the 75% growth the targets assume.

points.what: AOV fell 5.2% week on week to $87.91, though it remains 16.5% above the same week last year.
points.so_what: Orders grew faster than revenue this week, which is why revenue rose only 1.3% on a 5.1% order gain.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved 1.4 pp to 13.1%, down from 14.5% a week earlier and 14.5% last year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellation is worth about $905 of weekly revenue at current volumes.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 08 Jun 2026 was 9.7%, up 0.3 pp on the prior week but down 0.6 pp year on year.
points.so_what: Return behaviour remains better than last year, so order quality is not offsetting the cancellation improvement.

points.what: New customer signups were 244, up 1.2% week on week and 3.8% year on year, against orders up 89.3% year on year.
points.so_what: Order growth is running far ahead of new customer growth, so volume is leaning on the existing customer base.

summary.headline: Record week: orders 1,030 and revenue $78,682, both ahead of target and above their 8-week range; Q2 closed 100.7% of target but the year is behind.

points.what: Orders reached 1,030, up 5.1% week on week and 89.3% year on year, outside the 8-week range around the 939 average.
points.so_what: Order growth is running ahead of the 75% growth the targets assume for the year.

points.what: Revenue was $78,682, up 1.3% week on week and 124.3% year on year, against an 8-week average of $70,390.
points.so_what: The week finished $5,515 above its revenue target, at 107.5% attainment.

points.what: Q2 closed at 100.7% of the quarterly revenue target, $6,522 above the full-quarter target of $884,086.
points.so_what: The quarter is complete and delivered, after Jan to Apr fell behind target and May and Jun came in ahead.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue of $1,606,165 is 96.8% of target, a shortfall of $52,476.
points.so_what: A strong final week of the quarter has not closed the gap to the full-year target.

points.what: Orders hit 108.2% of the weekly target (1,030 vs 952) and revenue 107.5% ($78,682 vs $73,167).
points.so_what: Next week's targets step down to 936 orders and $58,879 of revenue.

points.what: QTD revenue finished at 100.7% of target, $890,608 against $884,086, with no weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Q2 is closed ahead of target by $6,522, the second consecutive month delivered above target.

points.what: YTD revenue is behind at 96.8%, and $2,282,637 remains over 27 weeks to reach the $3,888,802 full-year target.
points.so_what: That requires $84,542 of revenue a week, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $71,736.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate is reported for the mature week of 08 Jun 2026; the two most recent weeks are not yet mature.
points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week cannot be judged yet, so read 9.7% as a two-week-old signal.

points.what: The cancellation rate moved 1.4 pp week on week to 13.1%, beyond the 1.0 pp threshold for a notable change.
points.so_what: At about $905 of revenue per percentage point, this is a meaningful improvement in order quality.

points.what: Both orders (1,030) and revenue ($78,682) sit outside their 8-week ranges, above averages of 939 and $70,390.
points.so_what: This is a step above recent weeks, so it should not be assumed as the new baseline against next week's lower targets.
